visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A male speaker with glasses, grey hair, and a black button-up shirt stands centrally. He holds a small black remote in his right hand, gesturing with it as he speaks. The background is a vibrant digital landscape from the game Animal Crossing, featuring a pumpkin patch, wooden fences, and a cartoon character standing in the distance under bright, flat lighting. (2) The scene cuts to a digital document screenshot showing a scientific report from the journal 'Current Biology.' The text is dense with technical terms. The speaker is briefly shown in a corner inset, still gesturing with his hands to emphasize the academic achievement. (3) The visual transitions back to the main speaker, who uses animated hand movements to describe three types of animals. Transparent graphics of these creatures—brachiopods, phoronids, and bryozoans—are overlaid near his hands as he points to them in the virtual space. (4) Detailed diagrams of phylogenetic trees and colorful chromosome maps appear, filling the frame. The speaker remains visible in a circular or rectangular overlay, pointing to specific colored lines on the chart that represent genetic data. (5) The speaker concludes by facing the camera directly, holding the remote and smiling slightly. Yellow and white text overlays remain constant throughout the video at the top and bottom of the frame.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Slogan]: 一滴藥水逆轉老花?挺健康揭真相. [Variety]: 不是陌生人? 他們是親戚!. [Subtitle]: 這是困擾了科學家一百年的懸案. (2) [Subtitle]: 而就在剛剛, 由臺灣中研院羅以君老師與第一作者 Thomas D. Lewin 領銜的跨國團隊終於把它給破了. [Variety]: 直接登上《當代生物學》期刊. (3) [Subtitle]: 三位主角, 第一位是有殼的「腕足動物」... 據說廣東人會吃的「海豆芽」... 第二位是住在管子裡的「帚蟲」... 第三位是長得像地毯、像植物的「苔蘚動物」. (4) [Subtitle]: 所以在一百多年前, 科學家就覺得他們一定是一家人, 統稱「觸手冠動物」. (5) [Subtitle]: 這次羅以君老師的團隊決定換招, 不看「字母」, 改看「整本書的裝訂」, 也就是「染色體結構」.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a high-energy male narrator speaking Mandarin with clear, professional enunciation. An upbeat electronic pop BGM with a strong, synthesized 4/4 beat starts immediately. A sharp 'ding' sound effect triggers as the first text overlay appears. (2) As the topic shifts to the scientific paper, a metallic 'whoosh' SFX signals the visual transition. The narrator's pitch variability increases as he emphasizes the name of the research team. The BGM maintains its steady tempo of approximately 128 BPM. (3) A sequence of brief 'pop' sound effects occurs as graphic elements of the three animals are introduced. The narrator's speech rate is fast and energetic, with very short pauses between sentences. (4) During the genomic explanation, a low-frequency 'thud' SFX accompanies the appearance of the phylogenetic chart. The BGM volume ducks slightly to ensure vocal clarity while maintaining the rhythmic drive. (5) The video concludes with a rising synthesizer stinger SFX and the narrator's voice ending on a confident, high-arousal note. The music fades out with a quick hard cut.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Linear: Hook -> Background Context -> Methodology -> Evidence -> Conclusion
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to educate viewers about a significant scientific breakthrough in evolutionary biology. It explains how a multinational research team led by a Taiwanese scientist used genomic sequencing and chromosomal structure analysis to solve a century-old mystery regarding the relationship between different animal groups.

high_inference.freeDescribe: The video combines gaming aesthetics with complex scientific data to make academic content more accessible to a general audience.
